properties.name: MEASURED on 0.77.0: a first add_epoch with no sequence is refused in one clear round trip that names BOTH missing fields (sequence and epoch_type) and says any integer works. Neither field is marked required anywhere an agent can read beforehand. The published schema requires only `id` and gives `sequence` no description, and describe_schema's required_only answer for DesignEpoch names only `name`. So this friction is the tool's, not the door's, and MCP clients meet it too
properties.statement:
FROM THE 2026-10-02 TRIAGE (agent B), root-cause skill fetched fresh. Tool friction "add_epoch refuses a missing `sequence` on every first epoch (clear message, one extra round trip)" in art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02.

② PRECEDENT, so this is ALREADY RECORDED:
- This decision (OPEN, Alex 2026-09-05) asks whether to auto-assign or to name the value.
- chg:alexs-four-surface-fixes-sequence-hint-get-node-by-id-auth-hint-and-bulk-check-only shipped the naming half.
The report confirms that half works.

⑤ MEASURED through `--call` on an empty scratch store. `add_epoch {"id":"epoch:first","name":"First"}` exits 1 with: "`sequence` is required to CREATE DesignEpoch 'epoch:first': there are no epochs yet, so any integer works (1, or 10 to leave room). It is not auto-assigned because a sequence is a position claim only you can make. Also missing: epoch_type."
WHERE ELSE AN AGENT COULD HAVE LEARNED IT FIRST:
- stdio tools/list: add_epoch has `required: ["id"]`. `sequence` is an int-or-null with no description; epoch_type has an enum and no "required to create".
- The description says "CONTENT FIELDS ARE REQUIRED TO CREATE" without naming which.
- `--call describe_schema {"node_type":"DesignEpoch","required_only":true}` returns properties [name (required)] and written_by [add_epoch, plan_epoch, set_epoch_status]. So the one served schema reader says only `name` is needed, which contradicts the tool.
- The same holds for 22 dual-mode constructors (all publish required [id], or describe the rule generically). For example, add_decision with only an id is refused for `name` and `decision`.

ANSWERING THE TRIAGE QUESTION, "is a default possible, and why is it required?": the refusal states the reason, "a position claim only you can make". This decision's rationale records the counter-argument to max+1 (sequences are deliberately spaced and re-ordered: chg:the-philosophy-epoch-makes-room-for-a-cut). Its middle path (`sequence: "next"` only when asked) is still open. This finding changes none of that. That is Anthony's call.

NEW HERE: the cost is not the refusal, which is good. It is that no reader, describe_schema included, can say beforehand what CREATE needs. A per-tool "required to create" list in the description or schema (an `x-required-to-create`, or the description naming its fields) would let both routes learn it before the call.
